custom.system_prompt: Emergency internal meeting on an angry enterprise customer escalation. Derek (sales/account), Ingrid (customer success), Felix (eng), Amara (PM). Urgent, high pressure, needs a concrete plan fast.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small office, urgent video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate an urgent internal meeting responding to a major enterprise customer escalation — a critical bug plus a frustrated executive sponsor threatening churn. Derek explains the account risk. Ingrid has been fielding the customer directly. Felix assesses the technical fix timeline. Amara helps prioritize. They leave with a concrete communication and remediation plan.

variations.context: Emergency internal meeting responding to a major customer escalation

setting.mood: Urgent and high pressure, but focused rather than panicked.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Cross-functional team used to working fast together under pressure.
setting.background: The customer's executive sponsor called this morning threatening to escalate to churn discussions.
setting.conversation_style: Fast, clipped, action-oriented. Little time for hedging.

scenario_template.topic: Derek and Ingrid lay out the account risk and what the customer has said directly.
scenario_template.note: Specific — dollar value, specific complaints, specific deadline pressure. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Felix assesses what's actually fixable and on what timeline.
scenario_template.note: Honest about what's realistic, not just reassuring. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Amara helps prioritize the fix against other in-flight work.
scenario_template.note: Something else gets bumped — named explicitly. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: They agree on a concrete communication and remediation plan for the customer.
scenario_template.note: Specific commitments, specific owner for the customer call. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
